rows.evidence: Q1: Material and Method and Results <U+2013> lateral samples with emitters collected from 14 farms in Canakkale, tested in the hydraulic laboratory at 50-300 kPa; Tables 2-7 report clogged-emitter rates, flow-pressure exponents and uniformity parameters (Cv, Us, Eu, Cu) by years of use.
rows.notes: The study reports its own laboratory data on emitter clogging and uniformity loss in drip laterals used 1-3 years (15.6% of 3-year emitters fully clogged at 100 kPa, Cv up to 31.5%), attributing clogging to inadequate filtration, Ca/Mg precipitation from hard water (Table 3) and operation at 40-70 kPa. It contains nothing on fertigation (no fertilizer injection is mentioned), nor on the soil-health effects named in the claim (salt accumulation in the wetting front, hypoxia, nutrient supply, environmental contamination). The only overlap is that drip emitters clog, but the study does not test fertigation as the cause of clogging, so it does not provide own evidence on the claimed effect of fertigation on soil health or on fertigation-induced dripper clogging.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a lab performance evaluation of used drip emitters from farms in Canakkale, Turkey; it concerns hydraulic performance and water-quality-related clogging, not fertigation or soil health.
